result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up review stayed focused on prior finding SV-02-001 and the directly touched provenance surfaces: selected-version rendering, version-switcher rendering, and the related client/server assertions for AC-2.2.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale: The producing-process provenance is now rendered in both user-facing review surfaces: the selected-version panel shows a `Produced by` row (apps/platform/client/features/review/artifact-review-panel.ts:76-86) and every version-switcher entry includes `Produced by` metadata (apps/platform/client/features/review/version-switcher.ts:107-120). The follow-up tests now assert that provenance is returned by the API and rendered in the client for current and prior versions (tests/service/server/artifact-review-api.test.ts:165-197,324-333; tests/service/client/artifact-review-panel.test.ts:30-62,182-212; tests/service/client/version-switcher.test.ts:85-104).

gatesRun.command: corepack pnpm exec vitest run tests/service/client/artifact-review-panel.test.ts tests/service/client/version-switcher.test.ts tests/service/server/artifact-review-api.test.ts --environment jsdom

mockOrShimAuditFindings: No production-path mocks, shims, or fake adapters were introduced in the touched follow-up surfaces; the fix is pure client rendering over the existing review payload contract.
Test doubles remain confined to fixtures and in-memory/test harnesses; no new fake provenance source leaked into production code paths.
additionalObservations: The follow-up change is narrowly scoped to rendering and assertions; I did not find a new regression on the touched surfaces.
`verify-all` still passes with the existing scaffold-only `test:e2e` skip message, so there is still no executable browser-automation lane beyond service/client and integration tests.
